concepts.quote: Use point(0.5, 0.5), or call setXscale(0, 512) and setYscale(0, 512) first and then (256, 256) is the middle.
concepts.why: The answer correctly locates and fixes the mistake for this given failing case, relating the scale calls (made first) to how the later point coordinate is interpreted, with (0.5, 0.5) as the default-unit-square centre and (256, 256) as the centre only after a 0..512 scale; it does not describe what the default window actually shows nor generalise to a class of error, so it is relational rather than L4.
The answer says nothing about the double type or floating-point behaviour.
